title: 8 Leadership Goals For 2026 | FranklinCovey
summary: 8 leadership development goals for 2026: Improve time management, listening, delegation, trust, emotional intelligence, mentoring, and more.
body_text: 8 Critical Leadership Goals to Set in 2026 Published: 1/9/2026 Table of Contents How to Turn Leadership Vision Into Actionable Goals 8 Critical Leadership Goals Improve Time Management Strengthen Trust-Building Interpersonal Skills Lead Through Change With Intention Delegate With Purpose and Confidence Communicate With Greater Clarity and Impact Develop Future Leaders Through Mentorship Improve Strategic Execution Strengthen Team Alignment Advance Your Leadership Through Focused Goals Leadership is not a passive trait; it’s cultivated through deliberate action, continuous growth, and actionable goals. Leadership goals involve intentional behaviors, skills, and habits that leaders commit to improving over time, driving both personal and organizational success. These goals ensure that leaders evolve alongside their teams and remain effective in navigating challenges in the workplace. According to a study conducted by PwC , which analyzed over 1.5 million goals set by 12,000 employees across various industries, employees who set at least four daily goals per week were 34% more likely to achieve their key performance indicator (KPI) targets compared to those who did not. This statistic highlights the power of setting clear, intentional goals—especially for those in leadership positions. Rather than happening by accident, effective leadership is built through ongoing, purposeful development. To invest in that development, leaders need to start with a plan that outlines top ambitions and desired outcomes. These leadership goals are essential for driving organizational performance, enhancing team engagement, and ensuring long-term success. Key Takeaways: Leadership goals are objectives set to hone key skills, including time management, communication, and decision-making. Consistent development of leadership capabilities is vital, as leadership success is shaped through deliberate practice—not by chance. How to Turn Leadership Vision Into Actionable Goals To drive leadership success, leaders must start by setting clear goals that align with both personal growth and organizational needs. These goals help leaders focus their energy, prioritize effectively, build trust with their teams, and ultimately strengthen performance across the board. Leadership goals provide a measurable framework for growth, ensuring that leaders can make intentional decisions each day and track long-term improvement. The process of turning leadership vision into actionable goals can be broken down into a few key steps: Start with one Wildly Important Goal® (WIG ® ): Focus on the one goal that will have the greatest impact on organizational performance and that cannot be achieved without concerted effort. By zeroing in on a WIG , leaders can ensure they direct their efforts toward what matters most. Define high-impact behaviors (lead measures): Instead of focusing solely on outcomes, lead measures help leaders focus on the daily behaviors and habits that truly drive progress toward the ultimate goal. Understanding the power of lead measures helps leaders prioritize the most important behaviors, rather than getting completely caught up in the daily whirlwind of operations. Create a visible scoreboard: By leveraging a scoreboard , leaders and their teams can track progress toward their Wildly Important Goal in real time—increasing engagement, transparency, and accountability. This visual representation of progress keeps everyone aligned around the end goal and focused on making visible progress. Implement a cadence of accountability: Schedule regular, structured meetings to assess progress, review the scoreboard, and plan next steps. Establishing a cadence of accountability by holding weekly sessions ensures every team member feels accountable to their results and that everyone is on the same page. 8 Critical Leadership Goals Having a framework for achieving top initiatives provides leaders and teams with a roadmap to success. But before you can follow that map, leaders need to select their leadership goals based on their current role, the needs of their team, and their personal development priorities. Below are eight critical leadership goals leaders may consider setting for an outstanding 2026: 1. Improve Time Management Effective time management is an essential leadership skill, particularly when facing rapid change and uncertainty. Today’s great leaders have to balance numerous priorities, both urgent and important, and ensure that their time is spent on activities that yield high value. The 5 Choices to Extraordinary Productivity ® methodology helps leaders choose their priorities with greater clarity and purpose, reducing the likelihood of becoming overwhelmed by urgent but less important tasks. For instance, leaders who take Choice 1: Act on the Important, Don’t React to the Urgent ® to heart are able to prioritize high-value outcomes, even when seemingly urgent distractions come into the mix. The Time Matrix® below can help leaders distinguish between important and urgent tasks, enabling leaders to make better decisions about how to effectively allocate their time. Time management isn’t a new skill, but leaders can leverage new technologies to assist them in mastering it. In 2026, embracing AI in the workplace will allow leaders to automate routine tasks and focus on strategic decision-making. AI-driven tools can streamline operations and enhance clarity in project management, making it easier for leaders to maintain focus on high-impact work. Strategies: Leverage AI When Appropriate: AI is increasingly becoming a valuable tool in leadership, allowing leaders to automate routine tasks and focus on higher-value work. Leveraging AI for work and administrative tasks, such as scheduling, data analysis, or communication management, helps leaders reclaim valuable time for strategic thinking and decision-making. Leaders who embrace AI-driven tools can improve productivity and free up their time for more impactful work. Make Room for the Big Rocks: Outlined in Choice 3: Schedule the Big Rocks, Don’t Sort Gravel ®, leaders must learn to prioritize the most important tasks—the “big rocks”—and allocate time for them before anything else. By putting your most significant responsibilities at the top of your to-do list, you ensure that key priorities are never sidelined by minor distractions. This choice helps leaders create a disciplined, results-driven approach to their schedules. Be Mindful With Emerging Technology: Technology can be a huge asset when used intentionally, but it can also be a source of constant distraction. Choice 4: Rule Your Technology, Don’t Let It Rule You ® emphasizes the importance of setting boundaries with technology, such as managing notifications and limiting time spent on digital devices, so that leaders can remain focused on their most important tasks. Leaders who can take control of their technology will be better able to stay on track and maintain focus throughout the day. Remember to Recharge: Leaders often face the risk of burnout due to the demands of their role. Choice 5: Fuel Your Fire, Don’t Burn Out ® encourages leaders to focus on their own well-being by setting aside time for rest, recovery, and activities that recharge them. By maintaining energy and avoiding burnout, leaders can sustain their performance and effectiveness over the long term. By integrating these choices into their daily routines, leaders can not only improve their time management but also ensure that they are leading with clarity, focus, and intention. Organize your workload effectively and achieve your top priorities in 2026 when you download our guide, Manage Your Time Like a Pro: 7 Tips For Doing What Matters Most . 2. Strengthen Trust-Building Interpersonal Skills The first job of a leader at work or at home is to inspire trust. It’s to bring out the best in people by entrusting them with meaningful stewardships, and to create an environment in which high-trust interaction inspires creativity and possibility. — Stephen R. Covey While technical skills are often thought of as a prerequisite for leadership promotions, human skills are just as important, if not more important, for effective leadership outcomes. The ability to listen actively, show empathy, and manage relationships effectively is vital to fostering engagement and trust within teams. Despite a recent drop in employee engagement , with only 31% of U.S. employees reporting that they are engaged at work in a recent Gallup survey, leaders can play a key role in improving engagement through the use of soft skills. These skills are crucial for interpreting data with context, managing uncertainty, and creating trust . Strategies: Request feedback to uncover interpersonal blind spots: Feedback is one of the most powerful tools for improving interpersonal skills. Leaders should actively seek feedback from their teams, peers, and mentors to uncover areas where they might not be aware of their impact on others. Asking questions like, “How can I improve the way I communicate?” or “Are there ways I can be more supportive to the team?” will help leaders identify areas for growth. Regularly requesting feedback helps leaders stay grounded and avoid blind spots that could hinder relationship-building and team cohesion. Additionally, incorporating feedback into their daily actions demonstrates vulnerability and a growth mindset—both of which foster trust and show that leaders are invested in their own development. Practice active listening and empathy: Active listening is the foundation of building strong relationships. Leaders who practice active listening demonstrate a genuine interest in understanding their team members’ perspectives, which fosters trust and collaboration. This requires not only hearing what is said but also interpreting nonverbal cues, such as body language and tone of voice, to fully grasp the message. In practice, this means avoiding distractions, maintaining eye contact, and reflecting back what has been said to ensure understanding. By showing empathy and listening with the intent to understand before responding, leaders can connect with their teams on a deeper level and create a supportive environment that builds rapport, reduces conflict, and increases mutual respect—ensuring that all voices are heard and valued. Engage in regular reflection: In addition to feedback and listening, leaders should regularly reflect on their interactions with team members. This could involve taking time at the end of each week to review key conversations, decisions, and interactions. Reflecting on what went well and where there is room for improvement helps leaders stay conscious of their behaviors and adjust accordingly. This practice not only strengthens emotional intelligence but also enhances self-awareness, a key component of interpersonal effectiveness. As leaders continue to cultivate interpersonal skills, they will be better prepared to lead through times of uncertainty, maintaining a motivated and engaged team while building trust. Learn to lead with humanity and strengthen team connections with our guide, 6 Key Communication Phrases to Build Trust and Inspire Your Team . 3. Lead Through Change With Intention A plan gives both leaders and teams a path forward in times of change. — Kory Kogon, Vice President of Content Development, FranklinCovey Change is inevitable, but it is how leaders guide their teams through it that determines success. Leaders must be adaptable, resilient, and able to maintain team morale during disruptions. By embracing a solution-oriented mindset, leaders can help transform challenging periods of uncertainty into new opportunities. A leader’s ability to stay calm, focused, and optimistic during times of change inspires confidence and drives the team toward success. When individuals can lead through change with intention, they help their teams stay aligned, maintain agility, and keep moving forward even when the road ahead is unclear. In a fast-paced, ever-evolving work environment, leaders who model flexibility and openness are better equipped to guide their teams through uncertainty while ensuring high performance and engagement. Strategies: Communicate transparently: One of the most important ways to lead through change is by communicating openly and honestly with your team. Leaders should share information about upcoming changes as early as possible, offering clarity on what will be different and why the change is necessary. Transparency helps reduce anxiety and prevents misinformation from spreading, fostering a sense of trust and ensuring that team members feel prepared for what’s to come. By addressing concerns and providing a clear narrative, leaders can help their teams feel more confident and aligned in the face of change. Start small: When faced with significant change, leaders can help their teams manage the process more effectively by breaking larger changes down into smaller, more achievable steps. This makes the change feel less overwhelming and creates a clear roadmap for success. Additionally, leaders who set clear milestones and celebrate small wins along the way will build momentum and reinforce progress. Recognizing incremental achievements boosts morale and helps maintain motivation, even when the final goal feels distant. Celebrating small wins also helps teams feel a sense of accomplishment and reinforces that change is a process that can be successfully navigated. Create a safe environment to fail: During times of change, it’s crucial for leaders to encourage innovation and learning. Change often requires teams to adopt new ways of thinking and working, so leaders should create a culture that embraces experimentation and allows for mistakes. By normalizing failure as part of the learning process, rather than allowing stigma and fear to impede innovation, leaders can foster creativity and risk-taking to ultimately drive growth and improvement. Encouraging a “fail fast, learn quickly” mindset enables teams to adapt to change more rapidly and build resilience in the face of setbacks. Discover what’s driving today’s biggest disruptions for your workforce and the leadership behaviors that drive engagement and performance in our guide, The Energy of Change . 4. Delegate With Purpose and Confidence Effective delegation strengthens team capabilities, fosters trust, and prevents burnout. Leaders who empower their teams to take ownership of tasks help build a sense of responsibility and enhance overall team performance. Extending trust is a crucial part of this process; when leaders delegate thoughtfully, they build organizational trust that fuels collaboration and growth. Strategies: Match tasks to existing skillsets: Leaders should be strategic in identifying tasks that can be delegated to others. This requires a deep understanding of the team’s strengths, development goals, and areas of expertise. By matching the right tasks to the right team members, leaders ensure that their teams are operating at their highest potential. Empowering team members to own important tasks boosts their confidence and provides opportunities for them to develop their skills. Provide clear expectations: To set team members up for success, leaders must provide clear expectations about what needs to be done, how it should be done, and why it’s important. Clear communication helps to eliminate confusion and ensures that everyone is aligned on the goal and the desired outcome. Providing context around the task helps team members understand how their work contributes to the bigger picture, which reinforces a sense of purpose and accountability. Resist the urge to micromanage: Micromanagement undermines trust and stifles creativity. Leaders must resist the temptation to control every aspect of a team member’s work and instead empower them to take ownership of their tasks. Giving team members the freedom to approach challenges in their own way fosters independence and builds their confidence. When leaders trust their teams to lead and make decisions, it creates a culture of empowerment and mutual respect. Follow up to ensure accountability: While delegation involves trusting others to take ownership of tasks, it’s also essential for leaders to foster accountability . Scheduling regular check-ins, team meetings, or progress reviews will ensure that tasks are on track and that team members have the support they need. Following up at agreed intervals also reinforces the leader’s commitment to their team and helps maintain momentum, ensuring that tasks are completed successfully and on time. Accountability encourages responsibility and aligns team efforts with organizational goals. Foster accountability and inspire your team to achieve outstanding outcomes with our guide, 8 Ways to Boost Your Team’s Commitment to Goals . 5. Communicate With Greater Clarity and Impact Whether leading a team meeting, presenting to senior stakeholders, or writing a project update, leaders must convey ideas in a way that aligns people, drives action, and builds trust. Miscommunication can result in missed opportunities, delayed decisions, and confusion about priorities. In contrast, leaders who communicate with precision and purpose strengthen collaboration and accelerate execution. Remember: Your brilliant vision is only as strong as your ability to communicate it. An effective communication framework like Writing For Results ™ can help leaders craft messages that are structured, relevant, and audience-focused. These tools equip leaders to cut through complexity, connect with a wide variety of groups , and deliver messages that inspire confidence and clarity. Strategies: Practice structured messaging: Strong communicators organize their thoughts before speaking or writing. Using a simple structure—such as problem, solution, and action—helps ensure messages are clear and actionable. Whether you’re delivering feedback or pitching a new idea, starting with the “why” and ending with a call to action keeps conversations on track. Record and review communication for tone and clarity: Leaders can improve by listening to recordings of their presentations or meetings or have a trusted colleague review an email before it’s sent. This practice reveals filler words, vague phrases, or inconsistent tone. By reflecting on real examples, leaders become more intentional about how they show up in communication moments. Tailor communication to your audience: Great communicators adjust their approach based on who they’re speaking to. What resonates with executives might not be the same as what’s effective for frontline team members. Consider the audience’s priorities, language, and level of context needed. This practice shows respect for others’ time and enhances engagement. Invest in writing skills: In today’s digital workplace, written communication is more critical than ever. Leaders should refine their ability to write clear, concise, and persuasive messages that cut through digital clutter. While AI can provide a great starting point, it’s not a substitute for human connection and the unique point of view that each leader brings to the table. By improving communication discipline and practicing message clarity, leaders can increase alignment, build stronger relationships, and accelerate performance across teams and stakeholders. Download our guide, From Misunderstood to Magnetic: A Leader’s Guide to Clear Communication , to learn how great leaders can hone their skills and ensure their message lands. 6. Develop Future Leaders Through Mentorship One of the most impactful ways to build a strong leadership bench is through intentional mentorship. By creating a culture of coaching, leaders set in motion a ripple effect of capability and confidence across the organization. Effective mentorship doesn’t merely support individual development; it also reinforces your organization’s identity as one that values learning, accountability, and long-term succession planning. When leaders become mentors and consciously develop ongoing opportunities for learning, they help emerging leaders accelerate their development and better contribute to organizational goals. Strategies: Schedule regular coaching conversations: Consistency matters in mentorship. Establishing a regular cadence—monthly check-ins or biweekly touchpoints—helps mentees stay focused on their goals while giving mentors a platform to provide timely feedback. These conversations don’t need to be long, but they should be intentional and anchored in growth. Support goal setting and reflection: A powerful mentorship relationship includes helping mentees define clear, measurable development goals. Encouraging them to reflect on their progress builds self-awareness and resilience. Leaders should ask thought-provoking questions like, “What challenges are helping you grow the most?” or “Where do you want to stretch next?” Assign stretch opportunities: Practical experience is often the most effective teacher. Assigning mentees to lead a project, present to leadership, or navigate a cross-functional initiative gives them hands-on exposure to real challenges. These stretch assignments push them out of their comfort zones and develop both competence and confidence. Model the behaviors you want to see: Mentees learn just as much by observation as they do from direct coaching. Leaders should demonstrate the standards, values, and disciplines they’re encouraging in others. Whether it’s showing how to manage conflict or navigate strategic decisions, modeling is a crucial component of mentorship. Mentorship is not a one-time event—it’s an ongoing commitment to developing the people who will shape the future of your organization. Build a resilient leadership playbook for an uncertain future when you download our guide, Where Are All the Great Leaders? 7. Improve Strategic Execution Focusing on the wildly important requires you to go against your basic wiring as a leader to do more, and instead, focus on less so that your team can achieve more. — Sean Covey, co-author of The 4 Disciplines of Execution Strategic focus is the ability to prioritize what matters most and protect it from distractions. Many leaders are pulled in multiple directions, juggling competing priorities, endless meetings, and the pressure to produce immediate results. Without a clear focus on the most important goals, teams drift, resources are misused, and progress stalls. An execution framework like The 4 Disciplines of Execution ® helps leaders and teams achieve more by focusing on less. When leaders apply strategic focus consistently, they create clarity across the organization and ensure teams are working toward what truly moves the needle. Leaders can repurpose the steps they used to turn their vision into actionable goals to align their teams around their top priorities for 2026. Strategies: Define and commit to a single WIG: Leaders must decide what is most important—and make that priority visible and central to the team’s work. A WIG should be specific, measurable, and tied to high-stakes outcomes. When teams focus on one or two critical goals rather than many, they are more likely to deliver breakthrough results. Use lead and lag measures to guide focus: Strategic execution requires more than tracking end results. Leaders should identify lead measures—key activities that predict success—and monitor them regularly. This helps teams adjust course early and stay engaged in the behaviors that drive outcomes. Implement visual scoreboards to maintain alignment: Teams that see progress stay motivated. Using simple, visible scoreboards allows teams to track performance in real time, reinforcing ownership and commitment. Scoreboards should be easy to understand and updated frequently to reflect current performance. Maintain a cadence of accountability: Weekly team check-ins focused on commitments and progress help keep strategic goals top of mind. These sessions should be short, focused, and disciplined—each team member reports on past commitments, reviews the scoreboard, and makes a new commitment for the week. Leaders who practice strategic focus bring clarity to complexity. By prioritizing what matters most and executing with discipline, they unlock higher levels of performance and alignment throughout their teams. Download our guide, Execute Your Strategic Goals and Create Breakthrough Results , and set the stage for a high-performance culture that consistently inspires teams to achieve more. 8. Strengthen Team Alignment Team alignment is essential to achieving consistent, high-quality results. When teams are aligned around shared goals, expectations, and roles, they make better decisions, collaborate more effectively, and deliver greater impact. However, FranklinCovey research shows that only 15% of employees can name their organization’s most important goals—revealing a significant disconnect between strategy and execution. Leaders play a pivotal role in fostering team development and alignment. By clearly articulating goals, creating shared understanding, and reinforcing accountability, they ensure that every team member is working toward the same outcomes. Strategies: Regularly clarify priorities and expectations: Clarity must be reinforced, especially in dynamic environments where priorities frequently shift. Leaders should take time during team meetings or project launches to review key goals and ensure each person understands their role in achieving them. Don’t assume alignment; make it explicit by asking questions, checking for understanding, and connecting the dots. Use team kickoffs and briefs to establish shared ownership: At the beginning of projects or strategic initiatives, leaders should host structured kickoff sessions. These sessions clarify objectives, roles, success measures, and timelines. When everyone starts with the same understanding, teams can execute with speed and accuracy. Establish shared language and decision-making criteria: Alignment improves when teams use a common framework for decision-making. Whether it’s evaluating trade-offs or agreeing on criteria for prioritizing tasks, a shared language and established processes for making decisions will accelerate alignment and reduce friction. Reinforce alignment through regular feedback and course correction: As work progresses, leaders should review whether efforts are still aligned with goals and make real-time adjustments. Feedback loops, both formal and informal, will help teams stay agile and stay focused on what matters most. Alignment isn’t a one-time event—it’s an ongoing leadership discipline. When leaders create an environment of alignment, they empower teams to move faster with greater confidence. This alignment drives consistency, improves execution, and ensures that individual contributions ladder up to enterprise-wide success. In a rapidly shifting workplace, ensure your teams are aligned and inspired to achieve your top initiatives when you download our guide, Mobilize Your Team to Deliver Breakthrough Results . Advance Your Leadership Through Focused Goals Leadership growth doesn’t happen immediately, nor is it a one-time event. Instead, it’s a continuous journey that requires consistent practice, reflection, and intentional goal setting. By focusing on these critical leadership goals, leaders can begin 2026 by cultivating the skills needed to drive team engagement, performance, and long-term organizational success. Effective leadership directly impacts trust, engagement, and performance. Leaders should assess their strengths, role expectations, and team needs when selecting the goals they wish to pursue. By choosing a few goals to focus on at a time, leaders can make meaningful, sustainable progress. body_text: KORU Medical Systems Receives FDA 510(k) Clearance for Delivery of RYSTIGGO® (rozanolixizumab-noli), Expanding Label for FreedomEDGE® Infusion System January 29, 2026 4:05 pm EST Download as PDF MAHWAH, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- KORU Medical Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: KRMD) (“KORU Medical” or the “Company”), a leading medical technology company focused on the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of innovative and patient-centric large volume subcutaneous infusion solutions, today announced that the Company received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for use of the KORU Medical FreedomEDGE® infusion system to deliver RYSTIGGO® (rozanolixizumab-noli), a therapy commercialized globally by UCB, Brussels, Belgium ( www.ucb.com ). The clearance for the FreedomEDGE® label includes indicated administration by a healthcare professional, increasing flexibility and access for patients living with generalized myasthenia (gMG). RYSTIGGO® is a novel biologic approved to treat adults with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG), a rare, chronic autoimmune disorder that affects communication between nerves and muscles.¹ RYSTIGGO® is administered as a weekly infusion of 3mL-6mL of drug over 15-30 minutes for 6 weeks, with subsequent treatment cycles based on clinical evaluation.¹ “With this new FDA clearance, we are proud to further our leadership in the rapidly growing large-volume subcutaneous infusion market, with our ninth subcutaneous drug clearance," said Linda Tharby, KORU Medical’s President and CEO. "Expanding from home administration into clinic-based care highlights the versatility of our Freedom Infusion System to deliver life-changing therapies wherever patients are treated. This clearance aligns with our strategy to extend the Freedom platform to more drug therapies, more settings, and more patients.” KORU Medical’s Freedom Infusion System enables, simplifies, and enhances the delivery of large-volume subcutaneous drugs. Supporting drug products with various requirements for viscosity, flow rate, and delivered drug volume from 5mL-50mL+, the Freedom System is market proven with: 15+ years of patient self-administration in the home 45,000+ patients and over 2M infusions annually2 97% adherence rate3 and 9 on-label subcutaneous drugs distributed across 30+ countries About KORU Medical Systems KORU Medical Systems develops, manufactures, and commercializes innovative and patient-centric large volume subcutaneous infusion solutions that improve quality of life for patients around the world. The Freedom Syringe Infusion System (the “Freedom System”) currently includes the Freedom60® and FreedomEDGE® Syringe Infusion Drivers, Precision Flow Rate Tubing™ and HigH-Flo Subcutaneous Safety Needle Sets™. The Freedom System, which received its first FDA clearance in 1994, is used for self-administration in the home by the patient and/or delivery in an ambulatory infusion center by a healthcare professional. Through its Pharma Service and Clinical Trials business, KORU Medical provides products for use by biopharmaceutical companies in feasibility/clinical trials during the drug development process and, as needed, is capable of customizing the Freedom System for clinical and commercial use across multiple drug categories. title: Nabis Expands Offerings to Retailers, Driving Cannabis Wholesaling Standardization with Tech and Logistics
body_text: Dutchie to Partner With Nabis on New Tech Integration Offering, While Embarc Dispensaries Taps Nabis’ New Centralized Distribution Service SAN FRANCISCO--( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Nabis , the leading licensed wholesale platform for the cannabis industry, announces a milestone development in cannabis supply chain management with the introduction of retail partnerships to their expansive ecosystem. The wholesale pioneer has kicked off this announcement with two new partnerships: a tech-integration collaboration with Dutchie , the industry’s most widely used point-of-sale platform; and a centralized distribution solution for Embarc , one of California’s fastest-growing cannabis retailers. “Nabis’ mission has always been to provide scalable, compliant solutions that drive growth and efficiency across the cannabis market,” said Vince C. Ning , Co-CEO and Co-Founder of Nabis. “We see this expansion in our services not only as a collective investment in the digital and operational infrastructure of the future of cannabis retail and its community, but also as a shared vision of elevating the industry’s standards and business practices across the board.” Since its launch in California in 2017, Nabis has been at the forefront of solving complex wholesale distribution challenges—the addition of retail partnerships now takes its commitment to innovation one step further and bolsters the company’s 2024 expansion into New York and Nevada. The first retail-facing partnership Nabis is launching is with Dutchie, on a tech-integration collaboration, aimed to empower retailers with technology that aids their purchasing, inventory management and data-driven decision-making. By incorporating Dutchie’s Point of Sale (POS) system with Nabis’ wholesale Marketplace platform , the partnership enables retailers across the market with an industry first: integrated tech tools that inform product management based on real-time inventory insights and demand forecasts. With features like automated order suggestions, custom pricing insights and market analysis tools, the result is a smarter, smoother supply chain for retailers. “The cannabis retail landscape is constantly evolving, and the ability to adapt quickly to market demands is crucial for retailers,” said Tim Barash, CEO of Dutchie. “This partnership is all about giving retailers the data and tools they need to remain competitive and efficient in an otherwise unpredictable industry.” Separate from their collaboration with Dutchie, Nabis is also partnering with one of California’s fastest growing retailers, on a new, centralized distribution solution. Previously, vendors who work with merchants like Embarc, which has multiple locations in one market, were forced to deliver products separately to each location. This collaboration with Nabis will give Embarc—and future retailers who use the Nabis Centralized Distribution Hub—access to one centralized storage facility for all inventory to be housed for delivery. Nabis’ 150,000-square-foot warehouse and fleet of over 100 vehicles will then ensure timely deliveries of product to each retail location, all while reducing transportation complexity and cutting costs. “We need a solution that allows our brand partners to scale with us in a way that does not overburden their distribution infrastructure,” said Jason Pitts, President of Supply Chain for Embarc. “Nabis’ centralized distribution solution creates operational efficiency for us and our brands while allowing our in-store teams to focus on maximizing the customer experience.” Nabis’ services will also help retailers aggregate their purchasing partners, enabling customized automation for buying, further ensuring retailers can maintain product variety while still meeting market demand. title: Static onboarding tours break. The real cost of maintaining them in 2026.
summary: A no-code product tour is cheap to build and expensive to keep. Here's the full picture of what those tours cost over time, and why the math has changed.
body_text: Onboarding tours are the most over-promised tool in the SaaS stack. Every vendor in the category sells the same dream: a marketer drags a tooltip onto your product, and a guided experience appears for every new user, forever. The tooltip part works. The "forever" part doesn't. We've shipped tours for years. We sell a tool that builds them. So this isn't a takedown of the category. It's an honest accounting of what they cost, because most teams underestimate the second half of the bill. The numbers nobody runs When a team evaluates a tours product , they look at the headline price (typically a per-MAU rate, with seats as a secondary line) and call it a day. That's the wrong number. The right number is the all-in cost of keeping the tours alive. A typical mid-market SaaS team builds somewhere between four and twelve tours in the first quarter after install. Half of them break inside six months. The breakage isn't always visible. A tooltip pointing to a button that's been moved still renders, but it points at empty space. The user sees a hint about the wrong thing. Now do the math. Twelve tours, six broken, each one needing fifteen minutes to investigate and rebuild. That's an hour and a half per quarter from someone's calendar. Cheap, until you multiply it by every tour you've ever shipped, every release that touched a UI element, and every team member who has to remember the toolset. We've seen support teams spend a full afternoon a week running this maintenance loop. That's $40K-$60K of fully loaded labor a year, before counting the hidden cost of users who hit a broken tour and walk away without saying anything. Why this happens The product is built on selectors. The tour says "highlight the button matching .btn-primary ." When engineering refactors the component, the selector goes stale. The tour points at nothing. You can mitigate this with discipline. Tag every element you'll ever target. Add data attributes nobody allows you to remove. Run a regression suite of every tour after every release. In practice, most teams don't. The team that built the tours moves on. The new PM doesn't know which selectors are wired into a tour. The frontend team refactors a component because that's their job, and a tour breaks somewhere in the long tail. Nobody finds out for two weeks. The mismatch is structural. The product is built continuously, by people who don't know the tour exists. The tour is built once, as a snapshot of a moment in the product's life. What changed in 2026 Two things made this worse and one thing made it better. The release cadence got faster. Most growing SaaS companies ship to production multiple times a day. Every ship is a chance for a tour to break. Five years ago you got a release every two weeks. Now you get one every two hours. The frontends got more dynamic. Component libraries, design systems, A/B testing tools, and feature flags all introduce conditional rendering that selectors can't keep up with. The button is sometimes there, sometimes not, depending on the bucket the user landed in. What got better is the alternative. Agents that learn the product by using it can re-anchor against behavior, not selectors. When the button moves, the recipe still works because what's recorded is "click the primary CTA in the billing card," not "click the element matching [data-testid='upgrade'] ." The agent re-resolves on every run. Selector-based tours from WalkMe and Pendo carry this maintenance burden by design. Someone on your side has to repair every break, every release, forever. Users hit the broken steps in the meantime and learn to ignore them. The Frigade Assistant takes a different approach. The agent re-resolves against the live product on every run, so there's no selector cached anywhere to break in the first place. The team gets the time back, and users get the right walkthrough. The honest take on traditional product tours Tours break, but that's the symptom. Products have outgrown the static-tour model entirely. Products today aren't static. They ship continuously, they branch by user role and plan, they surface different UI depending on what a user has already done. The experience a power user sees on a Tuesday afternoon looks nothing like what a new free-tier signup sees on Monday morning. The number of meaningful paths through your product has exploded. A static tour assumes one path, one layout, one audience. That assumption was strained five years ago. Today it's untenable. You can't hand-author a walkthrough for every combination of persona, feature flag, and onboarding state. You'd need a small team just to keep up, and they'd still always be behind. As products get more personalized and more dynamic, the maintenance curve for static tours goes vertical. The only exit is guidance that's generated and adapted at runtime, anchored to what the product actually looks like for this user, right now, not what it looked like when someone recorded a walkthrough six months ago. Tours are hard to maintain, and for modern products they were never going to keep up in the first place.

title: What is hotshot delivery? A deep dive for construction teams
summary: Construction teams and retailers need to keep up with project and customer demand. Here's what hotshots are, and why they're a must to out-do the competition in 2026.
body_text: In construction, timing is everything. If you have entire crews waiting on tools, materials, or replacement items, timelines come to a halt, and costs can run up quickly. That’s why construction teams are increasingly relying on hotshot deliveries to keep project timelines right where they want them. Hotshot deliveries, simple point A to B deliveries that cut out the pit stops, can be pre-scheduled, next-day, or even same-day rush. They’re quick to book and save project managers from having to pay out and reschedule dozens of workers. So whether it’s a replacement part or a pallet of materials needed within a few hours, hotshots have become a core part of modern logistics. What’s a hotshot? A hotshot is a dedicated, nonstop delivery that starts at pickup and continues until it reaches the final destination. Unlike FTL or LTL service , hotshots are not consolidated with other shipments. It’s fast and top-notch service, but it’s also ideal for shipping fragile items or those requiring special-handling. Hotshots are most used for same-day or next-day delivery, when speed is a top priority. Delivery times are shorter and more predictable, and construction teams can prevent downtime and overspending on labor resources. Same-day hotshot services are typically cheaper than the surcharges associated with rush parcel services or local couriers. For third-party platforms with hotshots baked into their offering, pricing is competitive and predictable for every hotshot booked. How hotshots work The process may differ depending on the provider, but typically, the booking process is quite straightforward: A delivery booking is placed on a platform that supports hotshots. A dedicated vehicle and driver are dispatched for immediate pickup. Once loaded, the order goes directly from the pickup to the warehouse, jobsite, or distribution point without transfers or detours. A quality hotshot platform will also provide live tracking, proof of delivery, and push notifications so bookers and receivers can stay looped in on the order status. This also makes it easier for crews to coordinate the unloading and storage of materials on active job sites. Common hotshot use cases for construction Now, you can understand why hotshot delivery plays a critical role in construction. Hotshot delivery vs. traditional freight options So, why hotshots over conventional freight options? To put it simply, hotshots save excess time and money where the conventional methods don’t. Traditional freight focuses on long-haul cost efficiency and works well in specific, non-urgent deliveries. But it also introduces terminal stops and longer transit times. Local courier services may offer the speed businesses are looking for, but often lack the capacity or equipment needed for large or bulky construction materials. That’s where hotshots come in. They live at the intersection of speed, expertise, and convenience. They can handle pallets, tools, and bulky items. And when timelines are tight, paying for speed is often cheaper than the extra overhead of delayed timelines. Large retailers with dozens to thousands of storefronts also rely on similar logistics to meet rising customer expectations for speed. Retailers face constant pressure to offer same-day delivery (often within hours) while managing inventory across stores and warehouses. That’s where van fleet hotshots come in. Offering to move products directly from store to customer, or between locations without delays, van fleet hotshots give businesses greater control than parcel or crowdsourced delivery options. title: FMCSA 2026 Broker Compliance Rules: Bond, BMC-85 and USDOT Changes
summary: FMCSA's 2026 rules are now in effect. Shorter bond windows, stricter BMC-85 trust requirements, and USDOT numbers replacing MC numbers. Here's your compliance checklist.
body_text: The New FMCSA Rules: What They Mean for Your Brokerage The 2026 Compliance Deadline Is Real If you've been operating under the assumption that there's always another extension, it's time to recalibrate. January 16, 2026 marks a new compliance date that may be final. The rule was originally effective January 16, 2024, with a phased compliance schedule. FMCSA subsequently extended the compliance date for all requirements to January 16, 2026, creating a single deadline. At the time of writing this, in early 2026, no further extensions are expected. Here's what's changing and what it means for your business. 1. Your $75,000 Bond Just Got More Serious The bond requirement itself isn't new, brokers have been required to maintain $75,000 in financial security since MAP-21 passed in 2012. What's new is what happens when your security drops below that threshold. Old rule: You had a 30-day grace period to fix drawdowns or replace your security. New rule: If your financial security falls below $75,000 and isn't replenished within 7 calendar days, FMCSA will suspend your operating authority. Your surety provider is now required to notify FMCSA immediately when this happens. This raises the stakes significantly for compliance. What This Looks Like in Practice Consider this scenario: You have a $75,000 bond, and a carrier files a claim against you for $20,000 in unpaid freight charges. If the claim is paid out of your bond, your available security drops to $55,000. Under the old rules, you'd have 30 days to either replenish your bond or obtain a new one. Under the new rules, you have 7 days. If you don't act fast enough, FMCSA suspends your authority, and you can no longer legally operate as a broker. What This Means for Your Business A single claim can create an operational crisis. One significant dispute, even a fraudulent one, can trigger a compliance emergency if you're not prepared. Your surety provider is required to report you. If your bond drops below $75,000, they must notify FMCSA. Excess coverage is the prudent approach. If you're operating with exactly $75,000 in bond coverage, you're operating with zero margin for error. Consider carrying $100,000 or more. The additional premium is modest insurance against operational shutdown. Speed matters. You need to know immediately if there's a claim against your bond. Learning about it two weeks later may mean you're already suspended. 2. BMC-85 Trusts Are Getting a Major Overhaul What's Changing Eligible trustees: Loan and finance companies are no longer eligible to serve as BMC-85 trustees. Going forward, only banks, qualified financial institutions, or entities meeting specific FMCSA criteria can serve as trustees. Acceptable assets: Trust assets must now be held in one of three forms: cash, U.S. Treasury bonds, or FDIC-backed irrevocable letters of credit. Liquidity requirements: Assets must be readily available to be liquidated into cash within 7 calendar days. Why This Matters Before these rules, many BMC-85 trust providers were using illiquid assets such as real estate holdings, private loans, or other investments that couldn't be quickly converted to cash. This meant that when a broker went under and claims needed to be paid, the money often wasn't actually available. FMCSA is closing this loophole. If you're going to use a trust instead of a bond, the money needs to be real, liquid, and accessible. What This Means for Your Business If your current trust provider doesn't meet the new requirements, you have three options: Switch to a compliant BMC-85 trustee that meets the new requirements Move to a BMC-84 surety bond instead of a trust Lose your operating authority when FMCSA determines your trust is non-compliant Option three is obviously not acceptable. But the transition isn't automatic—you need to take action. Important timing note: Beginning January 16, 2026, when FMCSA becomes aware that a trust provider may no longer meet the eligibility requirements, the agency will review and verify the provider's compliance. If the provider is determined to be ineligible, you have 30 days to obtain a replacement filing from a qualified provider. 3. The Unified USDOT Number System FMCSA has proposed phasing out separate MC numbers in favor of a unified USDOT number system. While originally targeted for October 2025, the agency has delayed implementation and will open the change for public comment in a future Notice of Proposed Rulemaking. When implemented, everyone will operate under a single USDOT number with a broker or carrier designation Current System Carriers have a DOT number AND an MC number Brokers have a DOT number AND an MC number The two systems don't always communicate effectively A bad actor can have their authority revoked under one number and establish a new identity under another New System One USDOT number per entity All operating authority, safety records, and compliance history attached to that single number Broker or carrier designation indicated within the USDOT record Significantly harder to "reincarnate" under a new identity Why This Matters for Fraud Prevention The MC number system has long been exploited by bad actors. When a carrier's MC gets revoked for safety violations or fraud, they can often form a new LLC and obtain a new MC number. Their problematic history doesn't follow them, meaning they get a clean slate. The unified USDOT system changes this equation. Everything stays attached to one number. If a carrier or broker has a pattern of problems, that history is visible and persistent. This also simplifies vetting. Instead of checking both MC and DOT numbers and attempting to reconcile the information, you'll have one authoritative source of truth. 4. Identity Proofing for New Registrations New applicants for USDOT numbers or operating authority (including brokers) must now pass an identity proofing process through FMCSA's Unified Registration System. What This Looks Like Personal ID verification (government-issued ID upload) Selfie matching to verify the applicant matches the ID Business documentation verification Financial review What This Means For legitimate operators, this represents additional administrative steps to obtain or renew authority. For fraudsters, this represents a significant barrier. The ability to create shell companies with fabricated identities becomes substantially more difficult when the system verifies actual identification against a live image. The Downstream Effect Fewer fraudulent authorities will be issued in the first place. The supply of clean, stolen identities that bad actors depend on will diminish over time. This doesn't eliminate fraud entirely. Criminals will still attempt to steal legitimate carrier identities. But it closes one avenue and raises the barrier to entry. 5. Stricter Enforcement on Surety Providers FMCSA now has the authority to suspend surety providers who fail to comply with regulations. A provider found in violation faces monetary penalties and a mandatory 3-year ban from providing broker or freight forwarder financial security. Why This Matters Surety companies have not always been diligent about enforcement. Some have been slow to report claims, slow to notify FMCSA of problems, or loose with their underwriting standards. Now they have significant exposure. A 3-year ban from the market represents an existential threat for a surety company specializing in freight. They're going to be more careful about who they bond, how quickly they respond to claims, and how promptly they notify FMCSA of issues. What This Means for Your Business Your surety provider is now motivated to enforce the rules rigorously. They're going to ask more questions during underwriting. They're going to respond faster to claims. They're going to be more aggressive about notifying FMCSA of problems. This is largely positive for legitimate brokers—it raises the standard for everyone. But it also means you need to choose your surety provider carefully. Work with a reputable company that has a strong track record in freight. Don't simply choose the lowest-cost option.
